As Quality Director, the disposition decision falls to me, and I want to make sure we have a thorough review before we close this out. Per our standard process, I'd like to walk through the updates from each area — process, laboratory, logistics, and customer compliance — so we can determine the right path forward. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Here are my process findings from the oven recorder and tray map review. After the temperature alarm, I traced the recorder data against the tray map. What I found is that exactly 700 fasteners from trays P17 through P23 were exposed to the out-of-range temperature period. The remaining 1,700 fasteners were within the approved cure profile throughout the run. Based on this, the affected 700 fasteners can be re-cured in Oven 2 for exactly 2 hours to bring them back into spec. I have not yet attached this review to the batch record, but I'm sharing it formally here so the group has the full picture for disposition. I'll make sure it gets attached to the batch record once we conclude.

transcript.text: Thank you, Caleb. That completes the process, laboratory, and logistics updates. I'll now provide my customer compliance update. I checked the customer's quality portal regarding the re-cure scenario Jonas has outlined for the 700 affected fasteners. The portal confirms that any re-cured fasteners require two things before they can be shipped: first, a customer concession must be obtained, and second, a Certificate of Conformance must be issued that specifically identifies the re-cure. This is a hard requirement from the customer side — without the concession and the re-cure-identified C of C, we cannot ship re-cured fasteners to the customer. I should also note that I have not yet added this portal confirmation to the customer file, but I'm sharing it formally here so it's part of the disposition record.
